title: Interactive retainer calcs and heuristics
body:
Quick scratchpad: interactive retainer — aim is a simple product for high-frequency, low-latency interactive apps (chat UIs, copilots) where customers want predictable spend and an SLA-backed latency subsidy.

Top-level idea:
- Sell a monthly retainer that bundles a fixed number of 'interactive credits' + an SLA subsidy that underwrites low-latency execution (i.e., we accept lower unit margin to guarantee <100ms token tail for small burst).
- Credits are consumed by tokens + realtime concurrency uplift factor. Credits expire monthly, with rollover possible as a paid add-on.

Primary use-cases:
- B2B chat widgets with high per-user frequency but bounded message sizes (200-800 tokens typical).
- Internal copilots (engineering/product) where teams prefer predictable invoices.
- Startups where commit signal (monthly retainer) unlocks reserved capacity / faster support.

Assumptions / primitives (back-of-envelope):
- GPU amortized infra cost (our internal reserved pool): $3.50 / GPU-hour (after commits/discounts) for inference ops (targeting quantized A100-equivalent).
- Average throughput target: 65k tokens / GPU-hour (works out to ~18 tokens/sec sustained per GPU if multiplexed; conservative).
- Pure variable cost per 1M tokens ~= (GPU-hour cost / tokens per hour) * 1e6 = ($3.5 / 65k) * 1e6 = ~$53.85 per 1M tokens (in infra).
- Add fixed infra overhead + ops/support/monitoring (say 20% uplift) => ~= $64 / 1M tokens.
- Platform margin target (hosted) target price for low-latency tiers: $0.09 per 1k tokens = $90 / 1M tokens (so ~40% gross margin vs infra).

Interactive credit model (sketch):
- Define 1 interactive credit = 1k tokens * latency multiplier. Latency multiplier = 1.0 for unconstrained, 1.5 for latency-backed (we reserve hot capacity).
- Example credit pack: 200k credits/month = nominally 200M tokens (if multiplier=1) but realistic consumption reduces it.

SLA subsidy calculus (how to price subsidy):
- SLA requires us to keep a small hot pool that has slightly higher cost (dedicated hot GPUs, or pre-warmed containers).
- Hot pool cost multiplier: x1.3 of baseline (reserve premium + dedicated memory + eviction insurance).
- If we allocate 10% of customer's nominal capacity into hot pool, the incremental cost per 1M tokens becomes ~$64 * 1.3 * 0.1 / 0.9 ~= small bump; we can amortize across retainer.
- Simpler heuristics: charge an SLA addon % of retainer (5–12%) depending on concurrency guarantee.

Concrete candidate tiers (quick):
- Interactive Starter: $499/mo -> 500k interactive credits (~500M nominal tokens), SLA opt-in at +8% of price. Good for early startups.
- Interactive Pro: $2,499/mo -> 3M credits, includes 3k concurrent session headroom, SLA included (99.9% p95 latency target).
- Interactive Enterprise: custom pricing, committed throughput + reserved hot capacity, rollover + premium support.

Amortization worked example (Pro):
- 3M credits ~ 3B tokens nominal (if 1 credit = 1k tokens). But practical token usage: average message 400 tokens => 3M credits -> 7.5M messages.
- If a team has 1k DAU message-senders hitting 3 messages/day => 90k messages/month. 7.5M messages covers ~83 months => obviously oversized if used naively; so we should calibrate credit sizing with conversation/session semantics, not raw tokens.
- Reframe: pricing should express credits in "conversational sessions" where 1 session ~ 3 messages each 400 tokens => ~1.2k tokens => 1.2 credits. So 3M credits -> ~2.5M sessions.

Sensible defaults / guardrails to avoid extreme arbitrage:
- Per-session floor: minimum charge of 0.5 credits per message regardless of tiny token count (avoid tiny prompt abuse).
- Burst protection: allow short bursts but throttle if sustained > X qps beyond reserved headroom, fall back to pay-as-you-go token pricing (higher unit price).
- Rollover cap: at most 20% of monthly credits can roll over to next month for non-enterprise customers.

Experiments to run (MVP):
1) Small cohort beta: sell 10 Starter packs at 50% discount in exchange for telemetry (session sizes, concurrency, tail latency).
2) Price sensitivity matrix: vary list price vs credits by 3 points to map elasticity.
3) SLA addon anchoring: show customers quantized headroom options (1k, 3k, 10k concurrent) with % surcharge.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to map credits to embeddings (if customers use both generative + embeddings heavily)? Do we weight embeddings differently (x0.3 credit per 1k embed tokens)?
- Is it confusing to express in "credits" vs stating sessions + token allowance? UX test needed.
- Legal: refund / dispute policy for unused credits.
- Billing: auto-topup vs overage invoicing preference survey.

Notes to self / quick heuristics: 
- If average message length > 1k tokens for a segment, upsell per-message addon instead of credits.
- For high-concurrency enterprise, prefer simple reserved throughput (rps) SKU instead of credits.
- Consider a "warmth" metric: percent of requests that hit hot pool; target >70% for SLA value to be realized.

Next steps:
- Wire up a simple calculator in Sheets to convert: monthly price -> credits -> sessions -> expected TCO and margin (input variables: gpu-cost, tokens/hr, average-tokens/msg, messages/day, DAU).
- Draft wording for product page + FAQ explaining credit semantics and rollover.
- Kickoff small beta (PRIC-342) with solutions eng for 8 pilot customers.

Related tickets/links at top. Leave this doc as the working scratchpad; will refine into a small spec for PM/Design once we have telemetry from the beta.

-- end scratchpad
